Heltec MP3

Pocket MP3 player for the Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V3 · OLED menus · PRG-button or 4-button control · wired or Bluetooth headset · Wi-Fi control panel
firmware v1.1.0 ESP32-S3 1264 KB works offline

1 · Flash the board

  1. Plug the Heltec V3 into this computer with a USB-C data cable.
  2. Click Connect & Flash and pick the CP210x / USB serial port.
  3. Wait for 100 %. The board reboots into the player.
Ready.

Won't connect? Hold PRG, tap RST, let go of PRG, then try again. Close Arduino IDE / serial monitors first.

2 · Controls

Just the PRG button (no extra parts)

A thin bar along the bottom of the screen fills while you hold PRG so you can feel the timing.

With 4 add-on buttons (each button: GPIO → button → GND)

ButtonMenus & filesNow Playing
UP GPIO4Up (hold = fast scroll)Volume + · hold = Next
DOWN GPIO5Down (hold = fast scroll)Volume − · hold = Previous
OK GPIO6Select / openPlay / Pause · hold = Controls
BACK GPIO7Parent folder / HomeBack to the file list

The screen turns off after the timeout you set (Settings). The first press only wakes it.

On the back of the board, FLT, DEMP and FMT go low and XSMT goes high. Most boards come with these bridged already. If you get silence, check the H1L–H4L solder pads.

4 · Bluetooth headset

The Heltec V3's ESP32-S3 chip only has Bluetooth Low Energy. Headsets stream music over Classic Bluetooth (A2DP), which the S3 doesn't have, so the board can't pair with a headset by itself. A KCX_BT_EMITTER transmitter module (a few dollars, V1.7 recommended) does the headset part. The player controls it over two serial wires, so you can scan, connect and forget headsets from the OLED or the web page.
KCX_BT_EMITTERConnect to
+5VHeltec 5V pin
PGNDGND
AUDIO_LDAC LOUT (or jack tip)
AUDIO_RDAC ROUT (or jack ring)
AGNDDAC AGND only (keep it off digital GND)
RXlevel shifter ← GPIO 2
TXlevel shifter → GPIO 3
LINKlevel shifter → GPIO 38

Level shifter: a 4-channel BSS138 board. LV = 3V3, HV = 5V, GND to GND. The KCX expects 5 V serial signals, and some people report problems running it straight from 3.3 V pins.

  • OLED: Home → Bluetooth → Scan for headsets. Headsets show up as they're found. Select one to connect. * means it's remembered.
  • Web page: the Bluetooth tab has scan, Connect buttons, the remembered list, "Forget all" and a raw command console.
  • Put the headset in pairing mode before you scan.
  • It remembers up to 10 headsets and auto-connects to the first one it sees. With none saved, it connects to any headset in pairing mode.
  • The 5V pin only has power on USB. For battery use, add a small 5 V boost board for the module.
  • Wired headphones in the DAC's jack still work, but Bluetooth audio lags slightly behind them.

5 · Wi-Fi control panel

  1. First boot: the player makes its own hotspot Heltec-MP3-XXXX, password heltecmp3.
  2. Join it with your phone. The control page pops up, or go to 192.168.4.1.
  3. Wi-Fi tab → Scan → pick your home network → enter the password → Save & restart.
  4. After that, open the IP shown on the OLED (Home → Wi-Fi) or http://heltec-mp3.local from any device on your network.

If home Wi-Fi is down, it opens the hotspot again after 15 s and keeps retrying. You can turn Wi-Fi off in Home → Wi-Fi to save battery.

  • Player: play / pause / skip, volume slider, play mode.
  • Library: browse the SD card, tap to play, upload MP3s from your phone or PC, new folder, delete.
  • Bluetooth: scan, connect, remember and forget headsets.
  • Wi-Fi: join or forget networks.
  • System: SD space, restart, and wireless firmware updates (use the heltec-mp3-app .bin).

6 · SD card

  • Format as FAT32 (cards up to 32 GB are easiest).
  • Copy .mp3 files in, or upload them over Wi-Fi from the Library tab. Folders are fine (Artist / Album).
  • Up to 256 items per folder. Folders show first, A→Z.
  • The title and artist come from the MP3's ID3 tags, or the file name if it has none.
  • No card at boot? The player shows the wiring pins. Fix it and press OK (or hold PRG) to retry.

7 · Menus

  • Browse music: walk folders and pick a song. The rest of that folder becomes the playlist.
  • Now playing: shows title, artist, a progress bar, time and track number.
  • Resume last: picks up the last song after a reboot.
  • Shuffle folder: shuffles the folder you're in.
  • Bluetooth: headset status, scan, connect, reconnect, forget.
  • Wi-Fi: on/off, IP address, network or hotspot name and password.
  • Settings: volume, mode (Normal / Repeat all / Repeat one / Shuffle), screen timeout, brightness, resume, re-scan SD card.

Settings are saved on the board and kept between power-ups.
